title: Recording against the clock in the 1950s
summary: Jones and King discuss rushed sessions, four songs in three hours, and studio rates then and now.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yeah. Oftentimes, you have to record fairly quickly. Today, we're dealing with... Time conscious. Today, we deal with multi-track recording, where groups take often days and months to record. In those days, you went into the studio, and if you didn't do four songs in three hours in one session, uh... That's it. You didn't get the job done.

You had to do it. They're looking at the clock constantly. They want to know how fast you're going to get it done and get out of it. They were walking about $12 an hour, and today they charge you $150 an hour, you know. It's a difference. And now they go in the studio nowadays and stay in there, and it's infinite, you know. But, uh, you had to get the whole ball of wax done, the rhythm, the arms, a whole lot of sound. Yeah.
